concepts.def: Group based on income and job

walkthroughs.body_html:
Social class is a group sharing income, job and lifestyle.

It's not just about cash — it's accent, education, area too.

• Working class — manual or service work, lower pay.
  • Middle class — office or professional jobs.
  • Upper class — wealthy, often inherited.

The ONS uses 8 official categories — reality is messier than 3 boxes.

Income = money flowing in each year.

Wealth = total value of stuff owned (houses, savings).

The richest 1% in the UK own more than the bottom 50% combined. 📉

mcqs.q: How did Marx define social class?
options: Marx defined class by occupational status like the Registrar General.
Marx defined class by how much money people earn.
By relationship to the means of production: the bourgeoisie own productive resources; the proletariat sell their labour. Class is a structural relationship, not just income level.

mcqs.q: What is cultural capital according to Bourdieu?
options: Cultural knowledge, tastes, and skills that confer advantage in education and society.
Marx defined class by occupational status like the Registrar General.
The amount of money parents spend on culture.
Marx defined class by occupational status like the Registrar General.
The literal spread of McDonald's restaurants worldwide.
The spread of fast-food principles (efficiency, calculability, predictability, control) across society.
